questions.knowledge_point: Determining the Image of an Object Formed by a Singular Transformation
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14009909/assets/db7d2b33f2badad28b754d4482047a33bb37469ed8b7b17859b10552840e2f51.png)

Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 4 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Which of the following is the image of the triangle shown above under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the image of the triangle under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of the triangle:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -6 & -1 \\ 4 & 12 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the image's vertices are $(-2,4)$, 
$(-6,12)$ and $(-1,2).$ Notice that all three points lie on the same line.

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Coordinates of an Image Formed by a Singular Transformation
questions.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 2 \\ 10 & -4\end{aligned}]
$$

A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(-2,1),(0,0)$ and $(2,2)$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the action of $T?$  

- $(6,-18)$
- $(-5,-20)$
- $(12,-24)$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the image of $S$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 2 \\ 10 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}12 & 0 & -6 \\ -24 & 0 & 12\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

  

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are  $(12,-24),(0,0)$ and $(-6,12).$ 

So, the correct answer is "III only."

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Type of Image Formed by a Linear Transformation
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14009909/assets/8978d3bb02b4032b6e3a8b4a85878db647eb8323ac5b0423b5a9a6fab121c7e7.png)

Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ -2 & -8\end{aligned}].
$$

What would be the image of the triangle shown above under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that for any linear transformation $T$ with associated $2\times 2$ matrix $T,$ we have one of the following three possibilities:

- If $T$ is non-singular, i.e., $det(T)\ne 0,$ then the image of a two-dimensional object is a two-dimensional object. In particular, the image of a polygon with $n$ vertices is a polygon with $n$ vertices.

- If $T$ is singular, i.e., $det(T)=0,$ we have two additional subcases:

- If $T$ has at least one nonzero entry, then the image of a two-dimensional object is a one-dimensional line segment.

- If $T$ is the zero matrix, then the image of a two-dimensional object is the point $(0,0),$ the origin of the coordinate system.

With that in mind, let's examine our transformation.

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}det(T) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ -2 & -8\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-8)-4\cdot (-2) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a singular nonzero matrix. Therefore, the image of the triangle under the action of $T$ is a line segment.

choices.value: A point, different from the origin
The origin $O$ of the coordinate system

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14009909/assets/0231cc5aaf661cc873f18ff676a03d66927be48b49d38649efc45860197d18c1.png)

Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

What would be the image of the quadrilateral shown above under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that for any linear transformation $T$ with associated $2\times 2$ matrix $T,$ we have one of the following three possibilities:

- If $T$ is non-singular, i.e., $det(T)\ne 0,$ then the image of a two-dimensional object is a two-dimensional object. In particular, the image of a polygon with $n$ vertices is a polygon with $n$ vertices.

- If $T$ is singular, i.e., $det(T)=0,$ we have two additional subcases:

- If $T$ has at least one nonzero entry, then the image of a two-dimensional object is a one-dimensional line segment.

- If $T$ is the zero matrix, then the image of a two-dimensional object is the point $(0,0),$ the origin of the coordinate system.

With that in mind, let's examine our transformation.

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}det(T) & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-1)-0\cdot (-1) \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a nonsingular matrix. Therefore, the image of our object under the action of  $T$ is a quadrilateral.

choices.value: A point, different from the origin
The origin $O$ of the coordinate system
